-Every noise you make, Granny WILL HEAR.  So when you drop something, she will come running.
-Playing on beginner will remove the creaky floors.
-You can tell if Granny has heard a noise, since she will be walking at a much faster pace.
-The game has you set up to be found. There are traps set up all around the house that will make noise if set off.
-Keep in mind, that if you play on any oher difficulty than extreme, you ARE faster than Granny, which should help in clutch situations.
-Look legitamately EVERYWHERE for items, here is a list of their uses:
Hammer - Planks in the attic, main exit
2 Cogwheels - Playhouse
Padlock Key - Main exit
Weapon Key - Safe in the old house
Screwdriver - Metal plate in old house
Melon - Guillotine
Safe Key - Safe in basement
Master Key - Main exit
Wire Cutters - Main exit, Attic, Basement
Winch Handle - Well
Follow these instructions, and you should be good to go.

Tip on how to win!
Enemies:
The jump rope girl: A trap, just stay away from her at all costs. She can't see you, but she can hear you.

The principal: Will put you in detention for increasing amounts of times depending on the amount of times you break the rules. He is the guy who whistles

Sock: I don't know much about him, but all I know is he'll disappear if you stare at him. (Don't quote me on that, Im not sure)

GOTTA SWEEP SWEEP SWEEP: Will sweep anything...and anyone. This guy could be your enemy, sweeping you to Baldi, or your best friend, sweeping you *away* from him.

Bully: He'll take one of your items in your inventory. He will not let you pass him if you are unequipped with any items.

Baldi: Baldi..oh, sweet ol' Baldi..He hears all the doors you open and gets faster with every question incorrect. 


Items:

Bsoda: Will push enemies back when used.

Quarter: Uses to buy things...duh

Principals Keys: You can get out of detention early using these.

Baldi Disorienting tape: Self-Explanatory, using this will disrupt Baldi's hearing for a limited amount of time, making him lose track of you, if he SEES you though, it may not work.

Ending:
Don't panic when you try to leave and the exit, well, won't let you exit. The bald maniac will block the first 3 exits that you encounter, but then the 4th will set you free

The jokes, the smiles, the laughs, the screams, the editing (GOD the long, long hours of editing); even if it's fun, after a while it drains you and leaves you depleted until you don't have much else to give. They live in a world of auto-scrolling, constant uploads, a million memes a minute.  It's easy to forget that behind all the media they consume, that there are REAL people working their butts off to produce it.  Demanding someone to stick to a rigorous upload schedule is just unrealistic.

Truth be told, if you wanted to return to Let's Plays, you could do so at a more relaxed pace.  I loved your old playthroughs of Outlast and The Evil Within when it was just you, the camera, and the game.   Your later videos are hilarious, but I know that editing in all the memes and hard cuts take a ton of work.  It's okay to go easy on yourself.  Or if your funds allow, hire a video editor to take on the load so you can breathe and enjoy life again.

The neighbour and his wife got caught in a car accident. Sadly the wife died. They also had two kids (a son and a daughter) who were arguing one day, unfortunately resulting in the son accidentally killing the daughter. (Apart of the missing children). Henry programmed the Marionette before Charlie died to protect her. But she was too late when she got to the body and her soul transferred into the Marionette. When Henry said "The darkest pit of hell has come to swallow you whole. So don't keep the devil waiting, old friend." He was referring to Ultimate Custom Night (Ultimate Custom Night is William when he's sent to hell to be tortured by Golden Freddy/Cassidy/Andrew). Andrew is one of the souls in Golden Freddy. Watch Game Theory if you don't know Andrew from the book series.

2: You may be wondering. "Why did Henry burn all of the animatronics?". Henry lured all the animatronics into the pizzeria and burned down the pizzeria with him, Michael and the animatronic all in it because Henry is one of the good guys here. All the dangerous animatronics in there were the last animatronics with souls that haven't been freed yet. He got them all together and burned them to finally free them at put their souls to rest. Michael was eternally angry at William for killing the kids so he was also a vengeful soul that got freed.

I hoped this helped you.

Knowing that this video was posted quite awhile ago, Cory won't see this, but for all who decide to play this game, during the salvage testing phase, DO NOT PAUSE THE SOUNDS CONTINUOUSLY AND FLIP UP YOUR CARD! It doesn't matter if you check 'no', 'yes' or 'maybe'. Just listen to the sounds to the end. If you're not comfortable with flipping your card up after the sound stops, shock the salvage. Then document your results and continue doing this until the last sound. Of course, pay attention to the salvage if he/she moves, since that's super important. Cory, I'm not sure if you know this but you have to play the red light green light game in order for Mr. tatters to get the freak outta your face. Basically, when the screen is green you can move. When the screen is red, stop. You have to try to tag him.

For Kiki, just stare at her until she disappears.

I think Chester comes alive at 1am and he basically chases you down. The words Chester Marathon will be written on the whiteboard. You have to basically avoid him at all cost, but be warned that he is faster than the player so slow him down by closing doors and making quick turns around corners.

About Maxwell, the creepy mannequin thing. He shuts off the power which signals his attack and the player must run to the circuit box to turn it back on. If the you aren't near the circuit box, use you flashlight (yes, there is a flashlight) to slow him down and reach the circuit box. You won't have to worry about him when the lights are on. He is found on the level 2 area and when he is near the player, clicking and squeaking can be heard because of his hinges. Just like Chester, he is faster than the player.

Now Emily is in area 4. The player must run away from her as she charges through the vent. She will play a game of hide and seek with you. If the player sees Emily, they must run into a room and close the door. At 6am, you have to find Emily three times before 7am or else she and the others will kill you. 

Weasl is another new character (he is very ugly, not gonna lie). If the player hears a music box, they must find it and unwind it or else Weasl will pop out of the box and kill you.

There is an Easter egg of you in the game (I don't know if you found it or not or know about it).

And if you wanna know about the ending, all I'll say is fire.

When it comes to sponsorships, you will get the oppurtunity to accept one every day. These provide amounts of cash depending on the day you acceot them. As you progress, sponsorships will offer you more money for advertisement around your establishment.

Basically, you can be greedy and in return suffer from RNG (Randomly Number Generated, for those who don't know) adverts which will make the game harder the more sponserships you accept, or not take sponsorships and the money to survive easier throughout the nights.

Interesting Trivia: Joey Drew is basically a corrupted version of Walt Disney, his speech at 4:40 is very similar to the kinds of stuff Disney himself believed in.
*1.* Walt Disney was really big on believing in your dreams. In the note, Joey Drew is also a big believer of believing.
*2.* IRL Walt Disney was not a big fan of dying, and got his body cryogenically frozen after death because he believed he could be brought back to life again someday. In the note, Joey Drew also talks about wanting to cheat death.


And more clues from the game hinting Joey Drew is based on Disney:
*3.* Henry's note at 9:37 is *very* similar to Disney's relationship with Ub Iwerks, the creator of Mickey Mouse. Henry is complaining in the note of how Joey keeps taking ideas. IRL Ub Iwerks was responsible for a lot of Disney's early success, including almost all of the "Silly Symphonies" cartoons from Disney. But he didn't get as much credit from it as he was supposed to, and Disney kept taking all the fame. And the more famous the cartoons got, the more demanding Disney became with Ub.
*4.* In the same note, Henry talks about creating a new character "people are going to love." IRL, Ub Iwerks created the Mickey Mouse that everyone came to know and love.

Cory! There's ANOTHER ending! Well...it's kinda secret, so it's not really an ending. You won't get a trophy for this. Ya know how you said you saw a voodoo board in the trailer? Well there is something you can do with it! Here's how to get it!
1: get the kid wizard book, and throw it at the cat clocks eyes. I don't know if you have to directly hit its eyes, but try to hit the clock at least. 
2: you're taken to the cat clock room. Below you there should be a giant clock hand. With it you can change the times on the clocks. Correctly turn all the clocks to the correct times, until all the cats eyes are illuminated. You should get a message from the cat with a broken clock.
THE MINUTE HAND ON EACH CLOCK CORRESPONDS TO THE LETTERS OF THE ALPHABET. You can only spell something out with the first 12 letters of the alphabet, please remember this! 
3: after you crack the code, get your book and hit it against the giant yellow flashlight behind the clocks.
4: this takes you to a voodoo board. Use the glass to spell out the code from the clock room.
I'm very sorry if I missed any steps, I got this from another play through on YouTube. Good luck Cory, and good hunting!

The cat clock, you need to hit it when you get all 7 endings. If you do, you get transported to a room with a bunch of cat clocks with no eyes, and one with partially open eyes. What you need to do, is grab the big hand under you, and move the hands on the cat clocks until their eyes open. If you manage to do that, some messages and a kid wizard book will appear. After that, read the numbers on the little hand on the clocks. It should spell out a message, which reads "baddadbadkid". Then, throw the book at the flashlight, and then it will take you to a room with a Ouija board. Move the cup over the letters that spell the code. You then get transported to a room with a monkey in it, hence " beware the cat and monkey tricksters ". That's all I got, hope you find this helpful.

'Stuck' Ending

'Killed' Ending

The child was being affected by the constant arguing between his parents. That’s why the rat exists. The child subconsciously creates the rat in his mind to distract him from the arguing, but at the same time, the rat is used as symbolism to portray the fear the child feels when he sees/hears his parents arguing. Notice at the end how the rat shows up when the child hears them arguing, and then it disappears when the parents come in the child’s room to check on him. The child is in desperate need of more attention and love from his parents. The developer did a great job.

My theory about this game
The child we play as has a broken family who fight and argue a lot (which explains the adults yelling part) , leaving the child mostly neglected (why we never "see" the parents) the family has a pet hamster or rat or whatever you want to call that thing. The child is lonely and to get a friend he keeps the thing with him all the time. But because of the neglect and broken family, the child sees his pet as an imaginary friend who'll act and behave depending on the child's mood. The child is hungry so BonBon (the rat thing) eats the cake. the child is scared and the rat becomes a monster, the child is concentrated while cleaning up and he imagines the rat helping him out. When in reality, its just a little pet helping the child as some say that animals are smart enough to know what happens around the family, and the rat just helps the little kid and acts like a normal pet at the same. The horrifyng look of the rat might explain the child's imagination and how he may feel the parents see him. an ugly, fat, angry, sweet but annoying rat due to the neglect and arguements

so a lot of people might not understand what actually happened. Basically, that modern building with the radio tower that Cory saw across the lake was Murkoff's new facility. They kept experimenting w/ the morphogenic engine and it was affecting the townspeople, making them crazy. The flashes of light were the engine. The engine caused Blake to have flashbacks, getting more frequent the longer he was there. Lynn was never pregnant. It was a psychosomatic pregnancy (google it)  like what happened to the women from the asylum. That's why Lynn said "There's nothing there" as she died. Anyways, Blake's flashbacks we're about his childhood friend Jessica and her death. Basically, Father Loutermilch was... doing bad stuff to Jessica. She ran from him and he ended up pushing her down the stairs and Blake saw it happen. Father Loutermilch covered up the murder by making it look like Jessica hung herself.
who else watched the whole livestream under a blanket in a dark room?  Edit: u guys must like the dark

So, in addition to what Elise said below here are more clarifications from random parts of the game: 
- Jessica, Lynn, and Blake were all friends as kids. Jessica knew Blake had a little crush going on with Lynn and teased him about it because the two were close friends. 
- The guilt Blake feels throughout the game is because had he not left Jessica alone, she would not have died most likely. 
- Jessica was killed by the father after Blake left, by accident. Yes, assume that he was that kind of priest. She fell down the stairs trying to get away from him and Blake stumbled in to see her at the bottom of the stairs and the priest at the top. The priest then convinces Blake that he was confused and later covers up the death by hanging Jessica's body to make it seem like a suicide. 
- Knoth, the cult leader guy, said at the end of the game that he killed all of his kids. That didn't mean that everyone in the town was dead; everyone in the town died Jamestown-style. It has to do with the reason why Blake and Lynn were there in the first place and what the guy who gave Blake shelter told him. Knoth had a problem of raping all the women and girls in the town because it was his right. He then aborted all of the pregnancies he caused cause "God" told him too because they would be the Anti Christ. The man who gave Blake shelter, his daughter was the girl who had made it back to civilization and was found dead and pregnant and was the reason why Blake and Lynn had come to investigate her mysterious death. Assume that all the pregnancies were aborted because he feared that the fetus that survived would bring about the end of the cult's reality. 
-The people in the woods who saw Blake as a messiah and crucified him were all people thrown out from the cult and blocked from reentering the town. They all have syphilis, which is because of Knoth. That is why they are ostracized.  
-Val is the name of the person who steals Lynn away and tries to seduce Blake. Val is referred to by the game devs as "they." Val, like Knoth, believes that Lynn's child is the Anti-Christ, but unlike Knoth, they want the birth to come forth. Completely irrelevant but a sick detail: if you look around when you finally get back to Lynn in the mine shaft, the Heretics, Val's group, are very much having sex. 
-Lynn is pregnant due to the experiment that is being run on the town. (See Elise's comment) This is where a bit of Outlast lore is necessary to understand this game because all 3 are interlinked. Murkoff's experiment from Outlast 1/Whistleblower has an odd side effect of cause hysterical/psychosomatic pregnancies in women -- their bodies think they are pregnant but they aren't but will go through the whole process. This is why in the earlier two games there are zero women present in the entire asylum despite their being an entire women's block. If you look at Blake's shadow when he is holding the baby right after it is born, there is no shadow for the baby. For a team that puts this much thought into its games, we are going to assume that this is not a mistake or something they conveniently left out. There was no baby; it was a psychosomatic pregnancy; Blake has been in the town long enough to begin to hallucinate like the rest of the cult members and thinks he sees a baby. 
- Jessica constantly running out of nowhere is usually the hint you get that either: you need to follow her to know where to go or that something is about to start chasing you. It just goes back to the whole thing of Blake needing to stay with her when the father tried to pull her away. 
- If you look back at all the recordings taken in the school, there is nothing to see, implying that all school sequences are Blake hallucinating, which would be a product of being exposed to the radio tower experiment being run on the town. 
- If you look at Jessica's neck when she prays at the last time you see her, her throat has been slit. Blake is praying with a dead girl. This happens before Blake is swallowed up by the light so we are going to assume that he is dead, making Blake the second Outlast protagonist that dies by the end of the game (the other was the journalist contacted in the earlier two games). 

You were completely right to compare this game to Dark Souls. Outlast games are complicated and difficult and they really only make sense when you really know the game, whether that be playing through the first two a couple of times to understand how the devs want you to behave and react as a protagonist or reading through all of the notes that appear throughout the three games. Mind you, people agree that the story line for this is a bit hard to get the first time around, especially with the bouncing back and forth between hallucinating school sequence and the town, but once you know that this is a part of the same universe as the previous two games and you have read all the notes thus far, it is easier to get an idea about what exactly is going on here. The devs designed these games so that you need to play them through a couple of times, sometimes to just explore the environment and figure out where you need to go, sometimes to get the storyline, and sometimes to figure out the most efficient pathing to take to complete the game. They are intended to be difficult and frightening, but the more you play it the easier it is and the more you can predict the scares. 

Maybe you'll consider getting some friends and trying out Outlast Trials when it's released (should hopefully be this year, 2022), where we will get to see another of the Murkoff Corporation's experiments. It's a group game, but I think you can play it solo, where you work to complete specific tasks.

Michael, as in Mike Schmidt as he claims himself to be in the Attic, is alive. Whatever brought Mike, the Ignited's, and the lore relations to FNaF where brought into existence with supernatural means.

Mike says he feels amazing. He isn't just some identity the player has when playing FNaF. He is alive and isn't just the animatronic's target anymore. The only reason he wants to kill Scott is because, well he made him with the soul purpose of being a blank slate.

Scott had the idea's around to make TSE and SL. Infact given how all the games shown are only FNAF 1-4, we can assume TSE now exists and the concepts for SL exist.

I have a theory. Mike Schmidt hasn't just become himself. He's the Mike that we see in TSE. Why? He has golden eyes. Anything under the name Mike has now formed into Real Mike.

The animatronics. I believe they aren't just "animatronic's" brought to life. They can appear in multiple places at once and Chica can phase through WALLS.

Michael is described as looking like he "escaped from a bon fire". All the animatronics came from this fire(hence "ignited").

What if...these creatures are demons? They don't refer to themselves(the monitors in the basement) as animatronics. They are sort of...evil creatures that manifest themselves at Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy, and Golden Freddy. They all came from a fire in the middle of the forest, a place where paranormal activity was sighted.

And so Michael kills Scott. Or...replaces him. Remember SL? One of the main attributes of SL is that the protag is worn by a endoskeleton. But as time progresses...FNaF is slowly coming to life. Michael says it's HIS game now, so Scott is no longer the creator.

So, at the end, what we hear escaping the fire isn't Scott. It's "Ennard". The smoking gun? The slow mechanical glitching in his voice towards the end.

So Scott and Mike switched places. Scott is now a robotic monster, and Michael is in control of the games now. And what does he do?

He cancels it.

Cory, for the second mission, here is some info.
When you sit down on the couch, you can view both Foxy and Freddy's positions. By pausing, this stops their movement, BUT it only does this for the animatronic you paused. This also keeps you from checking in the other animatronic, so pause wisely. Hide behind the door on the left side to avoid being seen by Freddy. Hide behind the door on the right side to avoid being seen by Foxy. To my knowledge, you CAN NOT hide behind the couch. Another tip is to check the middle door whenever you hear sounds of movement coming from it, as this indicates that Bonnie has moved. Now, Bonnie does not have a camera, so you must look through a keyhole in order to keep track of its position. IN THE CASE that Bonnie is too close to the entrance of the middle door, hide on the side of the door, preferably on the left side of the room behind the little stand, using that as cover. IT IS CRUCIAL that Foxy nor Freddy is in the room, as one of them(Freddy, most likely if you use the position on the left side of the middle door) will see you, and, thoroughly make you restart the whole process. I have no info on Chica, so I apologize. I am sure you will get it right with it, though. (Like so Cory can see this tip, please).

EDIT: Chica works like how it did on the first mission. In the case that Chica gets in, here is what will happen. Chica will stun you and immediately stop the TV, hindering your capability of viewing Freddy and Foxy. I also believe that the madame you play as will not have the ability to move. Chica is rare, as far as I know, and I have no inkling on how to stop its advance. However, chances are that Chica will maybe TRY to attack at least once or twice, so its threat generation would be rather low. All of these affects reverse after a while, and you will be back in the fight. If Foxy, Freddy, or Bonnie are near and enter while you are still in your incapacitated position, then RIP. 

As usual, Foxy is faster than Freddy, so a strategy that can be used is to pause one for a long duration of time, while the other one advances. That way, you can hide behind the right door(Foxy) or the left door(Freddy) without having to worry about the other animatronic attacking. When the hiding is done and the animatronic that entered the room is gone, it will restart from its starting position.
If I was in that situation and I saw an animatronic walking in my living room, I would’ve been halfway to Mexico by then.

Freddy is at the window, he'll try to peek in just shut the curtains.


Bonnie will knock on the door and open it afterwards, disable the lights and sit down until he leaves.


Chica will try to stun you so if you see her peeking through the closet disable the lights and DON'T pretend to sleep.


Foxy will appear under your crib and move upwards, once you see him next to your crib, pretend to sleep until you hear him leave.

I'll give you all the info on the demo, so listen up!

- Chica
For her, you keep the lights on at all times, if they shut off, rush to one of the doors and turn the lights back on.

- Foxy
Flash Foxy when he's at his door

- Freddy and Bonnie
They both work pretty much the same way,
Looking through the keyhole lets you tell when they are getting close to the door.
If they get a little..."close for comfort" then you need to hide behind the couch, don't even worry about the lights, that will affect nothing.

Once you're hidden behind the couch, you will see them pass by, once you know they're gone for sure, then you emerge from the couch.

- Misc.
The clicking issue is mainly a problem with Unreal 4, as for some reason it's clicking is really off right now.

So here's what I've found out

- Flashlight 
It's probably the more responsive of the click commands

- Getting up from couch
The place it seems to detect the clicks the most is actually double clicking on the couch itself.

- Freddy's door
Double clicking the door or pressing 'S' will let you back up from that door.

- Bonnie's door
'S' will *never* work, trust me, I've tried.
You can only double click the door to back up.

That's about everything you'll need to know.

**NOTE**
The demo is unbeatable, it's mostly about getting the best possible times/

SPOILERSish

Honestly, this game seems to be about a young girl who witnesses her best friends murder and is powerless to stop it. On the day of the funeral, she sits on the bench by the lighthouse and thinks "what-if" and you play her "what-if" story. "What if I could rewind time?" You then go through her story, her pain and guilt, in order to "cope" with her death or overcome her death. You think about the life and adventures you could have had; but no matter what, the pain of her death keeps returning to your mind (hence why Chloe won't stop dying and you have to keep saving her). The harder she fights it, the bigger the storm (her grief) gets. 

In the end, grief is the storm you have to face, and you must make a decision once and for all (a final binary choice regardless of what you've done). You can choose to keep pushing on and hurting everyone around you (storm) and yourself (nosebleeds), or go back to the beginning and accept what happened (Chloe's Death).

This game is such a fantastic explanation of the "The Author Is Dead" premise in the philosophy of art.  Coda neither creates games for an audience, NOR do his games relate to his inner state of mind.  They are simply creations he has made in the purest sense of the word.  So what you extrapolate from them can only be your own personal interpretation.  To project those interpretations back onto the author, to conclude that he must be depressed or happy purely because of how you view his work, not only undermines the work as something that can stand on its own, but actually insults the creator, by implying they are only capable of creating art under specific emotional conditions, which is only capable of reflecting said emotional conditions and nothing more.  

Coda is. Not. Depressed.  Davey is depressed, Davey is frightened of social interaction, Davey is fearful of how others see him. That Coda's games moved him so deeply says nothing about the author, and everything about Davey.  And in the end, Coda proves - even in spite of all Davey's attempts to the contrary - that we know nothing about him.  No matter how many games he makes, we will never learn a thing about him.  Because art is not a reflection of the author, art is something that stands alone and divested from the author.  His opinions mean no more than the viewers - indeed they mean even less, because they're tainted by the technical process.  The second a work of art is finished, the very second...the author is dead.

54:27 - I put a lot of drawings and sketches out on my blog for people to see.  I also have a sketchbook that stays with me, and there are sketches in there that are for ME, and no one else.  What "Davey" did by showing "Coda's" games is like if someone took that personal sketchbook, scribbled their own fixes and interpretations all over MY thoughts, and showed them to others without my permission.  I don't blame Coda for pulling away, and looking back at the other games, I can see him trying so hard to tell Davey to stop - he MADE the games unplayable, but KNEW Davey would just mod them to find his own deeper meaning.

At the same time, I think I understand Davey too.  There are so many people I admire, and want to get to know on an intimate level, and being a rather shy person sometimes, it would be great to "pick apart" something they create to reach that understanding, and to apply it to myself and understand MYSELF better.  But... that's not right.  Unless the creator invites you to do so, that's breaching so many levels of trust.

Not to mention, demanding more from the Machine.  Always more, where is more, give us more more MORE.  That kind of attention can cause the Machine to burn out, especially when that attention was unwanted in the first place.  Still, even those of us who create and share our work reach that burnout too, so when we have to pull back... it helps when people respect that.

I have two theories about this game.

1. It is actually about Coda and Davey and how their friendship ended because Davey kept trying to push Coda to make games for other people as well instead of himself.

2. Coda and Davey are actually two parts of the actual Davey. Coda is his artistic introverted side that just wants to make games.

Game Davey is his Extroverted side that wants to make games that others can play so he can get feedback and feel like he is accomplishing something.

The Coda side of him had a lot of ideas for games but wanted to keep them to himself because he was worried what people would think and so he kept only consulting himself.

Game Davey wanted to actually show his games to people so he made them more playable and showed them to others because he wanted feedback and to actually interact with others. 

The Coda side of him is constantly worried about what people think of his work and because of this it's haunting his creativity . Game Davey knows that it'll be okay and that he wants to show people his games because they make him feel good.
 
But basically because of this the real life Davey is experiencing artist's block as he struggles between making artistic games for himself or games for others. 

Of course a lot of this second theory kind of applies to the first one as well as for why the two stopped being friends, but really we won't know which one is more correct unless we actually find out the real story from the writer.

so as of 19:58 in this video I think I figured out how the totems can affect the future.

Some shared traits of all totems: All of the totems show a future that may or may not come true based on the player's choices. Almost any totem can be missed, and affect the player's future as much as looking at the totem would.

White; Fortune: these look like they show the best possible outcome from a choice you can make, as if to show the player that if that outcome comes to pass, they did all they could.

Yellow; Guidance: The most unknown to me of the five, my best guess is they show at what point in the game a choice will be made, perhaps used in combination with other totems to show the player when an important choice is going to be made.

Red; Danger: This acts similarly to the Guidance totems, but instead of a location a dangerous entity is shown, as if to show the player a threat they have the ability to avoid.

Brown; Loss: This and the Death totem act very similarly. They show the worst possible outcomes from a choice made in the near future. Loss occurs from a different character's perspective

Black; Death: Similar to the Loss totem, this will show the worst possible outcome from a choice, acting like an opposite to a Fortune totem. Death totem premonitions occur in that character's perspective.

All of the above are *NOT* facts and the above may change as the story progresses. However I will leave this comment unedited as to not make replies look idiotic.

I'm gonna be honest about FNAF. When I first came to the first game, I thought it was spectacular. The originality, the characters, the detail, the lore, the secrets, easter eggs, etc. Scott did an amazing job. FNAF2, I loved it also. I like how in a way it was different and how Scott trolled us into thinking it was a prequel till night 6. FNAF3 was also really good. But it was also very hard to beat. And FNAF4 made me think. It was an amazing game series and it hurts to watch something so loved and amazing to just leave. I loved how each character had it's own personality and how Scott breathed life into them. Scott's a Christian game developer and didn't do well in selling his earlier games like The Desolate Hope and The Pilgrims Progress. But FNAF gave him his big break. And being the good person he is, used a majority of the money to help those in need. 
I admit, the games do get a bit boring, but I'll never be bored with how much work was put into them. All the detail and how much time it took for him to make the right game for the stories to connect. And how fun they were to play and the joy I felt when I beat the FNAF2 impossible level in 40 minutes. (EAT IT MARKIPLIER!)  We owe Scott for being awesome. I will in a way miss those creepy, murderess robots. I hope Scott comments on this video like he did with the other. God Bless Cory, and God Bless Mr. Scott Cawthon. Until the movie           :,)

The game takes place in 1987, after the events of FNAF2. Mary fell asleep on the job at a robot factory, many months or prior to her job at Candy's. This led to several children being murdered in the robot machine RAT (maybe). He was supposed to be stopped by Mary, but she wasn't awake to do that.

The parts that are covered in blood were used to make the "toy" looking animatronics, hence why the Puppet points to them after the murder, in a seemingly "you did this to them" manner.

The children who died in the factory have haunted Mary for "killing them", even though RAT (maybe) was the one who did the actual crime. However, as we can tell from the cutscenes, there is no evidence that RAT did it because the cameras were not recording the instances. Puppet seems to represent Mary and her guilt, due to the "MY" and "YOUR" being used synonymously.

Almost 8 years later and this episode still hits like a sledge hammer. The music that plays when they discover Rachel’s body, or even the sinister feeling you get when you enter the party. The first song that plays is so fitting to the atmosphere.

I know this is late but as someone who has a chronic pain condition, this ep really hit personally. When William spoke about how one second could change an entire life, i couldn't help but tear up. I went sledding after being afraid, it was the first time i actually did something risky. Now, i live with constant pain every single day no matter what (severe nerve pain)

Chloe talking about her experience being paralyzed hit really deep for me. Though I'm not entirely paralyzed, I'm constantly in my bed, asking for help every second. When she spoke about how the first day was amazing, it hit again. Something as simple as just going outside for a moment feels like a great adventure just because of how isolated and unable i am. I really love how she talked about it, it really made me cry for a moment, she said everything i feel, even without being paralyzed.

I thank the creators so much for showing it right. I don't want to be lazy, unproductive, and treated like a baby; But it gets so bad to that point, where my boyfriend and parents have to care for me. The medical bills are insane and our insurance isn't great either, it's stressful for everyone in the family-- But it's harder for her and I'm so glad they expressed that. It truly made me feel seen. <3
